residue.text: Interface ablation must withhold only newly completed P1 registrations from P2 eligibility while P1 registers and P2 requests and delivers initially registered N2. Neither disabling a clerk nor stopping a parent qualifies. No available control isolates this connection; changing eligibility violates fixed constraints.

Predicted final (registrations,recognitions): intact (8,8); broken connection (8,2); functional disconnected co-presence (8,2); P1 alone (8,1); P2 alone (2,2). Broken and disconnected co-presence are diagnostic counterfactuals outside executable constraints, not observed trials.

Interaction hypothesis predicts withholding transferred eligibility preserves eight registrations but limits recognition to two. Opposing parent-only hypothesis predicts functional P2 still recognizes newly registered identities under that same isolated ablation. Such recognition would defeat the interaction account; stipulated eligibility forbids this separating intervention.

Feasible intact replay reads completion, request eligibility, delivery and dashboard ledgers. Burden: six registration-clerk ticks, six dispatcher actions, automatic server processing; record failures and duplicates. Count or timing disagreement defeats the candidate schedule. This probe cannot separate accounts agreeing on intact behavior; no feasible causal separating ablation is supplied.

Delay origin, later sender adaptation, empirical performance and global optimality remain unknown. Later adaptation is an unobserved hypothesis; no additional demand occurs here. Successful intact replay would not establish an observed interaction effect.

summary.text: Fixed goal: eight registrations and eight distinct sender recognitions by boundary 9 within six dispatcher actions. Six registrations and seven recognitions remain. Outputs are independently measured; requests and duplicates do not count as recognition.

Intact candidate validates N3-N8 at ticks 0-5; requests individuals N2-N5 at ticks 0-3, bulk N6,N7 at tick 5, individual N8 at tick 6. Finite-model predicted deliveries: N2-N5 at ticks 1-4, N6-N8 at ticks 6-8. Six actions achieve both counts of eight; execution is unobserved.

Closest rival uses routine bulk at ticks 0 and 1 with identical validation order. Stale N1 causes duplicate slots at ticks 1 and 3; seven new recognitions cannot fit into eight available slots after those losses. Compare distinct recognition and wasted slots.
